questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: In Europe, but still a different (academic) culture compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of information, but it was doable. Some things just first make sense when you have arrived, so with some aspects it is just 'trust the process'.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The orientation day at the host university was helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Again it was doable but of course it can seem difficult when you don't know what you can trust before you go there. There are a lot of opportunities, but a lot of places that are suitable for (Erasmus)students, know that they can take a lot of money. Be in good time and look at the different opportunities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The public transport system in Prague is quite good, so don't be afraid to look at housing outside the city center, as by my experience the housing price reflects the location.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: they have a very confusing system. It is not possible to see schedules for courses before the semester starts, so even though you try to plan what courses you want, you can end up re-doing it. The course registration can also be a bit confusing and they have like a 'trial' period, so you can try out courses before you decide - it can be both beneficial, but also confusing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have an Erasmus office that can help, but they are only open a couple of hours a week, and in the beginning many students need help. The Czech students that helps Erasmus students are very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up registering for ca. 50-60% of the courses I originally planned for. Either because they didn't fit to my schedule or just because I found others interesting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Just have in mind that it can be a slow, analogue and sometimes a bit frustrating/confusing process. People are there to help.
Also a lot of the offered courses are quite low number of ECTS-points, so it can be a puzzle to make a decent schedule at the same time as reaching the 30 ECTS-points for a semester. My advice it to take as many courses with high numbers of ECTS-points, so you in total have as few courses as possible. Many courses are doable during the semester, but the exam period is quite harsh with 6-7 exams in a few weeks (as I had).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: same level as at UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some courses really similar to UCPH, some not. Also there is quite a difference in the level of english by the professors - some more understandable than others, but you get used to it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Environmental issues, background examples and solutions
2. Exploring contemporary migration trends: Diasporas, Refugees and Environmental migration
3. Flood Risk Management
4. Fundamentals of Demography
5. High-impact Weather Phenomena
6. Hot topic of environmental sciences
7. Introduction to Polar Ecology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
1. and 7. were a lot more biology than I expected, so if you are not ready for that, I would say it is doable, but quite hard.
6. is a really nice course. It is about how nature is valued, and give different perspectives on it. It is a small intimate course, where debate and talk is a part of it. Really good and nice teacher.
4. is a pure demography course. It can be a bit tough, but it is really in the depth with a topic not really covered at UCPH.

questions.answer: do day trips, either on your own or with some of the orgnizations.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, I didn't engage a lot with local people, but the city is easy to find your way around in.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There are many restaurants with different cuisines and it is quite cheap to go out

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy the city, it is beautiful. especially outside the citycenter there are really nice areas to explore. It is a city you can easily walk around in and explore.
2. Dont get frustrated during the process, everything will work out.
3. Talk to people in your classes, you will get new friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It is nice to experience the academic differences on another university and nice to meet people from other places. Everybody is there to have a good time, so engage in them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier can be challenging, but you will get used to it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
